note: Learner-facing wording for the Cambridge objectives at Stages 4 and 6. The Year 5, 7 and 8 packs print their own 'What it means for you' column; Years 4 and 6 do not, so their overview showed Cambridge's text instead — curriculum prose written for adults, denser for a nine-year-old than a Stage 7 learner gets. These are AUTHORED BY EHEL ACADEMY, not Cambridge, and are shown alongside the official text rather than replacing it. The register follows the packs' own paraphrases, graded so Stage 4 sits below Stage 5's wording and Stage 6 between Stage 5 and Stage 7.

learnerText.4Rq.01: Make up your own questions to help you understand a topic.
learnerText.4Ri.01: Find the information, and the answers to your questions, inside the sources you are given.
learnerText.4Rc.01: Find things out by interviewing people, using a questionnaire, watching closely and measuring.
learnerText.4Rf.01: Sort what you find out and set it out in a simple chart or diagram.
learnerText.4Ap.01: Notice that people think and believe different things about the same topic.
learnerText.4Ad.01: Look at a chart or some numbers and say what they tell you.
learnerText.4Ac.01: Talk about why you do something, and how it affects other people.
learnerText.4As.01: Suggest things you could do yourself that would help other people.
learnerText.4Es.01: Talk about a source, and notice that whoever wrote it has their own point of view.
learnerText.4Ea.01: Say what you think about someone else's view, and give your reasons.
learnerText.4Fc.01: Say what you were good at in your team, and what you found hard.
learnerText.4Ft.01: Say how working together made the result better than working alone.
learnerText.4Fv.01: Talk about what you learned, and how your own ideas changed along the way.
learnerText.4Fl.01: Notice which kinds of activity help you learn best.
learnerText.4Cc.01: As a team, give each person a job so that you reach one shared result.
learnerText.4Ct.01: Bring your ideas to the team, and work well with everyone in it.
learnerText.4Mi.01: Present what you know about a topic clearly, and in a sensible order.
learnerText.4Ml.01: Listen to others in a discussion, then add your own ideas and questions.
learnerText.6Rq.01: Start to build your own research questions, with a little help.
learnerText.6Ri.01: Find sources for yourself, then locate the information and the answers inside them.
learnerText.6Rc.01: Use an interview or a questionnaire to test a prediction, or to start answering your research question.
learnerText.6Rf.01: Choose what matters, organise it, and record it in whichever way suits your findings.
learnerText.6Ap.01: Pick out the key points of different perspectives on the same topic inside one source.
learnerText.6Ad.01: Find simple patterns in a chart or in numbers, and explain what they show.
learnerText.6Ac.01: Explain what causes a local issue, and how it affects other people.
learnerText.6As.01: Suggest an action that would improve a local issue, and justify why it would help.
learnerText.6Es.01: Discuss a source by thinking about who wrote it and why, and say what it does well and badly.
learnerText.6Ea.01: Give your opinion of a source, pointing to its features and the arguments it makes.
learnerText.6Fc.01: Discuss the difference your own contribution made to your team.
learnerText.6Ft.01: Identify what is good, and what is hard, about working together for one shared result.
learnerText.6Fv.01: Discuss how new information, or other people's ideas, changed your own thinking.
learnerText.6Fl.01: Name the skills you learned or improved while doing an activity.
learnerText.6Cc.01: As a team, plan and share out the work fairly, thinking about who is good at what and how much time you have.
learnerText.6Ct.01: Bring ideas that will genuinely help your team, and work positively to solve the problems it faces.
learnerText.6Mi.01: Present your information clearly and in a sensible order, mentioning your sources where that helps.
learnerText.6Ml.01: Listen to ideas and information about an issue, then ask the questions that matter to it.
